newsitem.title: USA: HFS Inc. buys PHH Corp. for $1.7 billion; stock soars.
newsitem.headline: HFS Inc. buys PHH Corp. for $1.7 billion; stock soars.

text.p: Continuing its wave of acquisitions, HFS Inc., which bought the Avis Corp. car rental firm only a month ago, went shopping again Monday with a rich $1.7 billion deal to buy PHH Corp., a company with complementary real estate and automotive businesses.

Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS, which is also a hotel and real estate franchisor, said it would acquire PHH, a provider of corporate relocation and other financial services, for $49.50 a share, a 60 percent premium over PHH's closing price Friday.
Following the news, PHH's stock soared $17.375 to $48.125 on the New York Stock Exchange, while HFS slipped 37.5 cents to $73.75, also on the NYSE.
HFS said it would issue 23.2 million shares in exchange for PHH's 34.8 million common shares.
Based in Hunt Valley, Md., PHH handles car leasing, real estate and insurance services for 3,000 corporate and government clients that relocate their employees.
Wall Street analysts applauded the deal, noting it was unlike most acquisition, which can require a year or more of integration before earnings per share growth resumes.
"This deal is immediately accretive to earnings," said Michael Mueller, an analyst at Montgomery Securities. "It's a case where being part of HFS strengthens PHH and vice versa."
PHH, which has annual revenues of $600 million and earnings of $86 million, operates in the United States, Canada and Europe.

"PHH is a perfect strategic fit within HFS and represents our continued evolution into a global service provider for consumers, corporations and other organisations," said Henry Silverman, chairman and chief executive officer of HFS.

"In corporate relocation, our existing business combined with PHH's relocation and other real estate services will benefit the transferring employees of our corporate customers as well as our franchised real estate brokers," he said.
Silverman also said that PHH's fleet leasing will boost HFS's fleet business and its Avis rental car operations.

"It's a terrific deal, really from the perspective of both parties," said Mark Manson, an analyst at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. "There just seem to be a lot of ways these companies augment each other."
Among the links analysts cited is that between PHH's auto fleet management operation, which buys cars for corporate leasing, and Avis, which HFS acquired for $800 million last month.
"HFS continues to make smart acquisitions," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "This fits with their most recent acquisition of Avis."

At first, HFS and PHH will likely benefit on the purchasing side of the auto business, analysts said. "PHH buys 100,000 cars a year," noted Manson, ticking off volume purchase discounts as the most immediate possible synergies.
Another potential benefit is in the disparate customer bases of the two companies. PHH largely relies on corporate and government contracts, analysts said, while HFS tends to serve individuals.

But the most powerful of the integration opportunities may be in the combination of PHH's relocation and mortgage businesses with HFS's vast army of real estate brokerages, which include Coldwell Banker, acquired in May for $740 million, and Century 21 acquired last August.

HFS also owns real estate franchiser Electronic Realty Associates, which was purchased within the last year, and has a $625 million-plus acquisition of Indiana-based Resort Condominiums International Inc. pending, with closing due by the end of the year.

"PHH's relocation business is a very significant addition because that's how a lot of real estate brokers get leads," said Montgomery analyst Mueller. "Right now, PHH works primarily with brokers that are not affiliated with HFS."
In turn, HFS' real estate brokers offer a deep well of business for PHH's mortgage origination operation, currently 12th-largest in the United States.
HFS said it will take a one-time charge as a result of the PHH acquisition, which is expected to be completed in the first quarter next year.
The company said it has not yet estimated the amount of the charge.
PHH Chief Executive Robert Kunisch will join the HFS board of directors when the deal is completed.
